races.name: Visitwexford.ie Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Game Phoenix
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with five runs on Good ground this season, never winning but placing regularly; amateur rider Mr B T Stone carries 7lb claim and last ran 21 days ago — holds his position well in a prominent role that suits this tempo.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out, Game Phoenix arrives here fit on a 21-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions; yet to win in her last five starts, but that runner-up effort is an encouraging platform under a hefty 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Tingarran Express
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and confirmed pace-setter; the STYLE_FIT flag notes it is racing out of its natural role at OR 100, but here it simply leads — uncontested on Good ground suits, though at age 9 and off a 14-day turnaround it must last home.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a second three starts back, Tingarran Express arrives here after just 14 days and with experience over today's trip and going, though she remains yet to win in recent starts and a hefty 168 lb burden is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Room For One More
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained five-year-old with a recent second over course-and-distance on Good; sits prominently and that profile is ideal here, trainer in flying form at T14 11/37 and the 2m1f trip is well established.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out, Room For One More arrives here on a quick 14-day turnaround with her trainer firing at 30% recently, and she has experience of today's going; winless in her last four starts and a hefty 160 lb burden may count against her.

runners_data.name: Teagarden Jazz
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse wearing tongue-strap; has form in the 3s on Good ground but this compressed pack may force him closer than he wants, blunting his late effort — the hg:t notation suggests breathing was a factor previously.
runners_data.comment: Teagarden Jazz arrives here rated one of the field at the top of our assessments, has run over today's trip and going, and bounced back to finish third last time out after a difficult spell — the concern is that she carries a hefty 159 lb yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Cool Summer
runners_data.note: Consistent placer who prefers to be delivered from off the pace; two recent seconds on Good ground show she handles conditions, but the slow early tempo will require her to either push forward uncomfortably or face a very short run to the line.
runners_data.comment: Cool Summer has been consistent without a win in recent starts, posting back-to-back runner-up finishes, though earlier efforts of sixth and sixth suggest her form can dip; she has run over today's distance and going before, but 157 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Barrogstown Girl
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a single course win on Good in her history; amateur rider Peter Smithers claims 5lb, which helps at the weights, but her pattern of finishing in double figures on fast days suggests she needs a genuinely strong pace to get into it.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Barrogstown Girl does at least return after a 21-day break with going experience on her side and a second two starts back offering some encouragement, though carrying 156 lb for a mare ranked 12 of 17 makes further progress hard to foresee.

runners_data.name: Bella Union
runners_data.note: Strong place record at 10yo with two wins on Good in recent history and a second just 56 days ago — the longer fresher gap is worth monitoring, but the horse's tendency to settle and deliver a clean jump at the last suits when a mid-pack run is available.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time out makes Bella Union hard to fancy here, and our figures rank him well down the field; on the plus side, he has winning form in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: The Toothpicker
runners_data.note: Consistent fifth-placer at OR 87 who presses from a prominent position; trainer Budds has 2/3 in the 14-day window, runs often on Good, and the horse's record of tracking the pace suits this shape well enough to be competitive again.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, The Toothpicker does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a third last time out hints at some residual form; however, a weight of 155 lb and a ranking of eighth of seventeen suggest he faces a stiff task from the middle of the pack.

runners_data.name: Ballinearla Girl
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type at heart, though mapped closer because the field is saturated with closers — the STYLE_FIT discount applies; no wins in 14 runs on Good at this trip and the slow pace will not stretch the field enough for her to thread through.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning after a 49-day absence, Ballinearla Girl does hold distance and going experience, and a third three starts back shows she can get involved — but a ninth last time out and a hefty 152 lb to carry make progress hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Kinski
runners_data.note: A true rear-of-field horse who fades in finishes under normal conditions; the redistribution to midfield and the STYLE_FIT flag both warn against taking the mapped position at face value — the fade flag compounds the concern in a slowly-run race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 15 of 17 on our figures, Kinski's recent form — featuring a refusal — makes him hard to fancy despite having run over today's distance and going before, and returning on a workable 20-day break.

runners_data.name: Owl's Delight
runners_data.note: Prominent-positioned runner with a fade tendency flagged; six runs on Good without a win, falls and pulled-ups in recent form suggest confidence and fluency may be issues — needs a clear passage and clean round to feature.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and with a pulled up and a fall among recent efforts, Owl's Delight arrives on a quick 12-day turnaround carrying 149 lb, though an official mark of 81 leaves a little room, and our rating of 88 suggests he holds latent ability worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Monty's Way
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse displaced forward in this map; the fade flag and a 49-day absence add caution, and the form string 6P0-00 signals he is out of form — the slow pace will not help a horse needing a real gallop to land a blow.
runners_data.comment: Rated 98 in a field of 17, Monty's Way shaped as a significant threat on paper, but winless in his last five starts — including a pull-up — and returning after 49 days, the concern is whether that recent string of poor efforts signals a deeper problem.

runners_data.name: Another Blunder
runners_data.note: Hold-up type forced closer by field composition; five-year-old with an all-GOO record that shows finishing positions of 10, 8, 6, 13, 12 — improvement is required rather than hoped for, and the fade flag signals no late kick.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Another Blunder faces a stiff ask here; she has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 25 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh, but the consistent unplaced efforts make her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: At The Wings
runners_data.note: Placed to midfield from a natural hold-up style by redistribution; trainer Norman Lee has 1/2 in the last 14 days which offers a faint live angle, and the 7-7 recent finishes in handicap company at least represent consistency if not progress.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, At The Wings has at least run over today's trip and going before, though a weight of 142 lb is a stern ask for a gelding yet to show his best, and he remains on the retrieval end of recent form.

runners_data.name: Nukie's Artic
runners_data.note: 136-day absence is the dominant concern before anything else; the fade flag and hold-up style displaced forward compound the query — trainer McCarthy has been active (T14 3/14) but returning fresh in a 17-runner handicap off a long break is a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with two unplaced efforts among them, Nukie's Artic is ranked well below the principals on our figures and returns after a 136-day absence, making him hard to fancy; experience over today's trip and a mark of 82 are the main positives.

runners_data.name: Sidiriya
runners_data.note: Useful form at the lower end — has a second and a third in recent runs on Good — and while the redistribution applies, shorter recent absence (18 days) and positive finishing positions make this a mildly interesting outsider if the race falls apart.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 17 on our figures, Sidiriya is hard to fancy, her recent form showing a fall last time out and winless in her last five starts, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a second three starts back offers a crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Cowboy
runners_data.note: 420-day layoff is an obvious and significant query; has placed three times on Good but returns fresh from a very long absence into a competitive 17-runner handicap — trainer Winters has 0/3 in 14 days and only hg:p (cheekpieces) to spark a revival.
runners_data.comment: Phoenix Cowboy has run over today's trip and going before, yet arrives winless in his last four starts and faces a stiff test off 158 lb after a 420-day absence — rustiness is a real concern, though a rating of 96 suggests latent ability.

races.paceDynamic: Tingarran Express is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, with no serious challenger for the lead, should settle into a controlled, energy-conserving gallop from the front — a sustainable pace rather than a pressured one. Game Phoenix, Room For One More, The Toothpicker and Owl's Delight will push for prominent positions directly behind, creating a compact early order at the head of affairs without materially lifting the tempo. The bulk of this field are genuine hold-up types — Bella Union, Cool Summer, Teagarden Jazz, Barrogstown Girl and Phoenix Cowboy among them — who will find themselves racing closer than ideal in a compressed pack given the shortage of early pace, squeezing out their customary late runs. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can all sit at the rear in their natural position; Ballinearla Girl, Kinski, Nukie's Artic, Monty's Way and others mapped to midfield are genuine closers pushed forward against their instincts. With one front-runner dictating at a measured tempo on Good ground, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently in a genuine tracking role — those sitting second to fifth — who can travel into the race without expending energy and pounce before the true closers can generate their run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Hold, Smooth Dispatch
scenarios.trigger: If Tingarran Express sets a sustainable gallop and horses sitting second to fifth travelling easily inherit the race from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Tingarran Express controls without pressure, and the chasers immediately behind — Room For One More, Game Phoenix, The Toothpicker — travel into the race on the bridle before asserting as the front-runner fades; the measured tempo means their energy is preserved for the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Tingarran Express is allowed to dictate entirely unchallenged and the small field of prominent challengers fail to close the gap at the last.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to press Tingarran Express early, it finds a rhythm and idles into the finish at a speed no closer can match off such a modest gallop; prominent types who track but lack a finishing kick are left with a race that has been run to suit the front-runner throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is more contested than expected early and the tempo rises enough to string the field out and create a genuine closing run.
scenarios.body: A faster early fraction would play into the hands of a true hold-up runner who can pick through tired horses from two out; Bella Union and Cool Summer both have strong recent form sitting second and both possess the finishing resolution to benefit if the pace genuinely lifts.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Redistribution
scenarios.trigger: If several redistributed hold-up horses push forward out of position and create a falsely-run, stop-start race that scrambles the form book.
scenarios.body: Compressed midfield traffic and horses racing outside their comfort zone produce a rough-house finish where positional luck and jumping fluency matter more than class; a lightly-weighted improver hidden in the pack could emerge late.

watchPoints.text: Tingarran Express gets away entirely uncontested — if no horse from the prominent group pushes up to sit within two lengths before the halfway mark, the front-runner could steal a march that is never recovered.

Room For One More jumping and travelling — if the Mullins runner shows any hesitancy at hurdles or loses prominent position early, the race shape that most favours it dissolves quickly in a 17-runner field.

Bella Union's 56-day absence and age (10) — watch the market move and early jumping to assess whether the horse is returning fresh and ready or rusty; a clean round early would be a positive sign for the hold-up scenario.

Traffic risk from redistributed hold-up horses — Ballinearla Girl, Kinski, Monty's Way and others racing out of position could create significant midfield congestion from the third-last, obstructing runners trying to make ground on the outside.

Nukie's Artic reserve rider and 136-day absence — if the Reserve 1 jockey is a lower-claim amateur unfamiliar with the horse, combine that with the long break and treat any market support with great caution rather than following it in.

races.name: Treo Eile Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Mahler's Best
runners_data.note: Tendency to fade in the finish is a real concern over 2m4½f on Good; the hold-up style from Alex Harvey will demand a clear run in a big field, and the sim-going record (0 wins, 0 places in Good) gives little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and our rating of 89 ranks her eighth of seventeen, but she has run over today's going before and returns on a quick enough turnaround of 20 days; the 166 lb burden is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Ocean Of Dreams
runners_data.note: Amateur jockey in a 17-runner heat is a significant tactical disadvantage; hold-up style makes positioning hazardous, and the form string of 6s and 8s suggests a horse finding its level rather than threatening.
runners_data.comment: Ocean Of Dreams has been winless in his last five starts, with an eighth and sixth his best recent efforts, and our rating of 86 suggests he faces a stiff ask from 165 lb here; the 30-day break at least means he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Boola Times
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe booked is a big positive in a competitive handicap; fading tendencies remain a concern, but recent Good-ground form (5th, 3rd) suggests she handles conditions and the shorter side of the trip suits better than longer tests.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Boola Times does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a third two starts back offers some encouragement, though the pulled-up effort three starts back and a hefty 162 lb ask remain concerns for a gelding rated 91 officially.

runners_data.name: Monntie
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner and its key pace-shaper; John Joseph Hanlon's four-year-old has raced consistently on Good ground (7/7 sim-going runners) but is technically racing out of natural role as a prominent type rather than a dominating front-runner — Danny Gilligan must gauge how much to give early.
runners_data.comment: Placed two starts back, Monntie arrives on a handy 21-day break with going experience in her favour, yet she remains yet to win in her last three starts and a ranking of eleventh of seventeen suggests she faces a stiff task here.

runners_data.name: Toon Town
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose true style is obscured here — in reality likely to be shuffled into midfield or further back given the field size, making his winning position hard to secure; the one win from eight Good-ground starts came over 2m4f, so stamina and conditions are fine, but his chance hinges on finding daylight.
runners_data.comment: Toon Town won three starts back and returns fit on just eight days' rest, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; the risk is that his last two runs have been fifth and seventh, suggesting he needs to bounce back to that better form.

runners_data.name: Ardera Gun
runners_data.note: 126-day absence is a genuine flag; Richard Deegan rides a horse whose form away from the track includes a pulled-up run, and being a true hold-up type in a 17-runner field after a long break makes this an awkward assignment.
runners_data.comment: Rated 100 by us and ranked third of 17 in this field, Ardera Gun has strong claims on today's going, which he has encountered before, though 126 days off and a pull-up last time make him a bigger risk than his mark of 85 suggests.

runners_data.name: Tomas O Maille
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a form string of 9s and pulled-ups; Phillip Enright takes over but the record shows a horse that has not threatened in a long time — the hold-up style leaves him dependent on others' misfortune in a big field.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of seventeen on our rating, Tomas O Maille has distance and going experience to call upon and returns on a sharp nine-day turnaround carrying 155 lb, yet his recent string of pulled-up efforts and tail-end finishes makes it hard to trust him yet to score.

runners_data.name: Ray Gun
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a patchy form string (0P-P96) and only five Good-ground runs sampled; Daniel King rides a horse whose true nature as a hold-up type means he will struggle to find his stride in time in this field, even though he is mapped to midfield.
runners_data.comment: Ray Gun has run over today's trip and going before, but his recent record gives little encouragement — winless in his last five starts and twice pulled up in that sequence, though 14 days' rest and a rating of 91 suggest connections retain some belief.

runners_data.name: Bruise Hill
runners_data.note: Consistent fader in the finish on Good ground (0W0P in five Good runs) and a hold-up style pushed into midfield — Kevin Healy's claim helps on weight, but the profile screams out of-the-frame finisher in this company.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 17 on our figures, Bruise Hill is hard to fancy at the weights, though he has run over today's going before and returns after a 31-day break at least fresh.

runners_data.name: Miss Guiry
runners_data.note: Multiple starts at this sort of level with results of U000-S tell a damning story; hold-up style and a tendency to fade make it very hard to construct an optimistic case, despite Peter Smithers' claim.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 12 of 17 on our figures, Miss Guiry is hard to fancy, though she has run over today's going before and 15 days since her last outing suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Nothing Da Now
runners_data.note: Maike Magnussen's six-year-old has finished 7th or lower in most recent starts; a hold-up horse forced towards the middle of a big pack, with ordinary Good-ground figures (3 from 7 in any sort of placing position), faces a stiff task.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pulled-up and two seventh-place finishes among her recent efforts, Nothing Da Now faces a stiff task carrying 153 lb and ranked well below the top-rated runners on our figures, though she has experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Tedworth
runners_data.note: Solid 2m4f form on Good ground — 15 from 15 sim-going — with a win and a place in recent history; John Shinnick rides a hold-up horse whose best chance comes if the pace is genuinely strong and the field spreads, though the 43-day gap and out-of-role mapping temper confidence.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win four starts back but has since posted a fourth, an unseating, and a seventh, making his recent profile patchy at best; has run over today's trip and going, and 43 days between runs leaves fitness an open question at 153 lb.

runners_data.name: Seekthisfairland
runners_data.note: A 75-day layoff and a form string of 0s and finishing positions in double figures; the four-year-old has not placed in four Good-ground outings and the tendency to fade makes this a tall order.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to win in recent starts, Seekthisfairland returns after 75 days carrying 148 lb, and with just four runs to his name he remains open to improvement as connections look to unlock his potential.

runners_data.name: Annie Questions
runners_data.note: Amateur rider in a 17-strong handicap; the hold-up style and fading tendency are compounded by a record showing only one win (over shorter on different ground), and the 42-day absence adds another question mark.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift of the field on our figures, Annie Questions has managed just one win in her last five starts and her recent form figures make her difficult to fancy; some encouragement that she has run over today's going before, but that is about as far as it goes.

runners_data.name: Friar Hogan
runners_data.note: Reserve 1 status means raceday confirmation needed, but if he runs the second place at 2m4f on Good ground (2/20f/GOO) is the standout piece of recent form here; his hold-up style is natural and a strong pace would play to his strengths.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Friar Hogan does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a second two starts back shows he can threaten at this level, though the dead weight of 165 lb and a ranking of sixth of seventeen suggest he faces an uphill task here.

runners_data.name: Getaway Charlie
runners_data.note: Reserve 2 status is the primary caveat; the ten-year-old carries top weight but has a win and two places in Good-ground chases at staying trips — if he gets in and the stamina test increases, his experience counts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Getaway Charlie nonetheless heads this field on ratings and brings distance and going experience to a testing 170 lb burden; 24 days between runs looks sharp enough, and the form needs turning around, but he is the one they all have to beat.

runners_data.name: Dark Berkshire
runners_data.note: Reserve 3 and therefore unlikely to run; a third placed effort at 19f on Good is reasonable, but the fading tendency and hold-up style in a 17-runner field make this a horse to treat with caution even if declared.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 16 of 17 on our figures, Dark Berkshire is hard to fancy despite having run over today's distance and going before; a third two starts back offers faint encouragement, but 146 lb makes life no easier.

races.paceDynamic: Monntie is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to pressure her — she can dictate from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop over the 2m4½f trip on Good ground. With Wexford's flat, right-handed circuit and a field this large, a controlled lead at a sound but not frenetic tempo is the most likely race shape, putting a premium on horses that can travel close enough to strike when Monntie's advantage is tested approaching the last. The field contains a significant surplus of hold-up types — Toon Town, Ray Gun, Ardera Gun, Tomas O Maille and several others are genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because they cannot all get to the rear in a race this competitive; Toon Town and Ray Gun, both progressive-enough types, are best placed to forge close to the pace if they choose to adapt. This shape — a single uncontested front-runner at a comfortable tempo — overwhelmingly favours horses with the tactical speed to sit handy in the first half-dozen and pounce in the straight, rather than true closers who will be stranded wide or in traffic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Monntie Controls, Handy Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Monntie leads unchallenged at a fair clip and the race is decided in the home straight by the horses who tracked her.
scenarios.body: Monntie sets a steady but genuine pace and the well-positioned hold-up/prominent horses who have managed to travel in the first five or six gain a decisive advantage turning in; the combination of Good ground and a manageable tempo rewards tactical agility over raw stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Increases, Stayers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens significantly in the middle stages — perhaps from Toon Town or Ray Gun forcing their way up — and the race becomes a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop would string the field out and expose weaker finishers, bringing genuine stayers and horses with distance form to the fore; the longer trip and Good ground would then reward horses proven at 2m4f-plus who can sustain their effort.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Monntie Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Monntie's front-running is so controlled that she conserves enough energy to simply resist all challengers up the straight.
scenarios.body: A race run entirely to her own rhythm would allow Monntie to steal margins at the hurdles and build an unassailable advantage before the chasing pack can close; her recent consistency on Good ground and tactical ease make this a genuine if minority possibility.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or traffic problems disrupt the handy horses, opening a late run for true hold-up types at the back.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires several redistributed hold-up horses — who are not naturally suited to sitting last in a 17-runner field — to somehow find clear daylight late, making it the least likely shape; even if the pace evaporates, genuine closers here have modest form figures at this level.

watchPoints.text: Monntie (Hanlon/Gilligan) dictating every yard from the front — if she is allowed a completely uncontested lead, her rivals face a tactical problem as early as the third-last hurdle.

Toon Town and Ray Gun, genuine hold-up types mapped to midfield, may attempt to push forward and force a pace injection mid-race — watch for either to move up unexpectedly in the back straight, which would materially change the tempo.
Friar Hogan and Getaway Charlie are both Reserves — check the final declarations; if either runs, their staying form on Good ground represents a live upgrade to the closers' section.

With 17 runners on a right-handed circuit, traffic and interference are a serious concern for any horse drawn wide or racing deep in the field — watch for early crowding off the bend that could end several hold-up horses' races before the halfway point.

Ardera Gun's 126-day absence and Seekthisfairland's 75-day break are the two most significant fitness flags in the field — both hold-up types who need to be near their best to have any chance in a race this size.

races.name: Treo Eile Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Lincall
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Ryan/Shinnick combination, solid record on Good ground with two top-six finishes at the trip, but returning after 93 days off and has never won; will need a clean passage in this big field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning from a 93-day absence, Lincall nevertheless got round for sixth after that pulled-up run, and his going experience plus a rating of 102 make him a genuine threat at the weights — though that layoff remains the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Chosen Princess
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner who can dictate fully; has placed once in five Good-ground runs and rates OR 93, but the STYLE_FIT flag suggests she may not fully relish being used more forcefully than usual — if she gets it her own way she is dangerous, but she has no wins to her name.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and clearly capable on her day, Chosen Princess has run over today's trip and going before, but winless in her last five starts and carrying 161 lb looks a stiff ask for a mare ranked sixth of seventeen.

runners_data.name: Torque De Lune
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type for Hanlon who handles Good well (5 from 7 in similar going), ran third over course-and-distance last time, and Gainford's claim could help at the weights; the unfinished efforts are a concern in a race where jumping is at a premium.
runners_data.comment: Torque De Lune has had a troubled recent spell — unplaced last time out, and unseated two starts back — and our figures rank her well below the field, making her hard to fancy at 160 lb, though she does return within a reasonable 26 days and has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Sharetheknowledge
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer who handles Good ground well and has two places from 15 similar-going runs; Conor Smithers takes 7lbs off and the trainer has no recent form to note, but the horse's style is perfectly suited to tracking Chosen Princess.
runners_data.comment: Sharetheknowledge has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 99 puts him firmly in contention from a field of 17 despite his 159 lb burden — the chief concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts, including a pulled-up effort.

runners_data.name: Corkbeg
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose true style sees him hunting off the back of the field, though the crowded map has him shown in midfield — Kelly's yard is in good recent nick (2/13 over 14 days) and the horse has placed twice on Good; nine-year-old carrying 152lbs needs things to fall right.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 12th of 17 on our figures, Corkbeg makes little appeal at 152 lb, though he does return on a quick turnaround with both distance and going experience in his favour.

runners_data.name: Balinaboola Steel
runners_data.note: Remarkable 14-year-old returning from 740 days off for Leahy; a natural rear-of-field type with one win and four places on Good over fences and hurdles, but the layoff is a massive unknown and his natural instinct to wait will leave him last of all in a 17-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and pulling up in each of his last two outings, Balinaboola Steel arrives after a gap of 740 days, yet he has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 108 marks him as the one to beat — fitness after such a lengthy absence is the obvious question.

runners_data.name: Scarlet Purse
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish and has a poor record in similar going (4/10), and her true hold-up style means she is unlikely to get a clear run in this field — difficult to fancy on current form or race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Scarlet Purse has a tough ask from 151 lb and ranks 13th of 17 on our figures, though she has run over today's going before and the 25-day break gives connections every chance to present her fresh.

runners_data.name: Sekakarma
runners_data.note: O'Keeffe rides a genuine prominent type with two places from ten Good-ground runs and was second and third recently; only nine days since his last run, but O'Keeffe's experience and the horse's consistency make him one of the main dangers.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but rarely out of the frame, Sekakarma arrives here fresh on nine days' rest with experience over today's trip and conditions, though a 151 lb ask gives the handicapper the edge against a gelding yet to find the winner's enclosure.

runners_data.name: The Ducks Walk
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse placed in midfield on the map due to congestion at the rear; Condon (5lb claimer) takes the weight off, and the horse has placed three from five on Good — needs clear daylight that a field of 17 may not provide.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, The Ducks Walk at least returns quickly on 15 days' rest and has experience of today's trip and going, though carrying 150 lb and rated 11th of 17 by our assessors makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Tantrum Boy
runners_data.note: Finishes tired in most runs and the hold-up style combined with the fade flag makes him hard to place in this scenario; Enright is a capable rider but four recent finishes of 8, 16, 11 and 4 show inconsistency, and the soft-ground form is irrelevant here.
runners_data.comment: Tantrum Boy has been winless in his last five starts, finishing fourth twice before that form tailed off badly, and our rating of 74 ranks him 16th of 17 here; weight of 146 lb adds further to the task, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Fenno's Soldier
runners_data.note: 1,345 days off the track is a catastrophic layoff concern regardless of any other factor; held up naturally and has only run on Soft previously, so Good ground here and a massive field on return from over three and a half years away makes this an extreme risk.
runners_data.comment: Fenno's Soldier has been off the track for over three and a half years, making him deeply unexposed and open to significant improvement, though he arrives yet to win in his last four starts and faces a stern test carrying 145 lb on comeback.

runners_data.name: Little Boy Sivola
runners_data.note: Rothwell yard in form (3/13 over 14 days) and the five-year-old has placed at the trip, but the P last time and three consecutive back-half finishes on Good suggest he does not quicken; blinkers fitted, which could spark improvement or cause jumping errors.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, including a pull-up most recently, Little Boy Sivola faces an uphill task here, though he has run over today's going before and 35 days between runs suggests he returns fresh; carrying 145 lb looks a stiff ask at a mark of 77.

runners_data.name: Inches Away
runners_data.note: Repeated finishes of 10th and 17th at short odds suggest a horse well below this level; the fade flag and poor going record (3/8 on Good) compound the concern, and Cashman's stable has no recent form noted.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 15 of 17 on our figures, Inches Away is hard to fancy at the weights despite having run over today's going before, with only a fourth last time out offering any crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Cruisin Susan
runners_data.note: Berry's nine-year-old has placed three times on Good including a third over 24f, and the 7lb amateur claim helps; her natural hold-up style suits a truly-run race, though the fade flag is worth noting against stronger finishers.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Cruisin Susan does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and was third two starts back, though eighth last time out is harder to ignore, and 140 lb adds further pressure on a mark of 72.

runners_data.name: Duke Otto
runners_data.note: Top-weighted runner at OR 98 with no jockey listed (possible non-runner risk); has placed four from fifteen on Good and won once, but recent form shows P, 4, 11 — the hold-up style and top weight make it hard to be enthusiastic unless the race collapses.
runners_data.comment: Duke Otto has run over today's trip and going, our rating puts him among the leading contenders here, and 36 days between runs suggests connections have had time to plot a comeback — yet winless in his last five starts, with two pulled-up efforts in that sequence, the worry is whether he retains enough ability to deliver.

runners_data.name: Rumble Demosa
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with only three runs for Griffin, all finishes of 11th, 7th, 7th on Good — consistent mediocrity so far; the yard has no recent winners noted and the trip (19-20f previously) is being stretched here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked ninth of 17 on our rating, Rumble Demosa does at least bring going experience to the table, though 158 lb is a sizeable burden and her recent string of unplaced efforts offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Warm In Gorey
runners_data.note: Rothwell's in-form yard (3/13 in 14 days) sends out this eight-year-old who has placed an extraordinary seven times from 15 on Good without winning; the tp headgear combination and consistent placed form at the trip make him a stalwart each-way type in any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Warm In Gorey has placed third three starts back and again four starts back, though back-to-back sixth-placed efforts since suggest he may be finding life harder; he has run over today's trip and going, but 164 lb is a stern ask.

races.paceDynamic: Chosen Princess is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and is expected to stride on from the outset, setting what figures to be a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 2m4½f trip on Good ground. With no other genuine front-runner to apply pressure, she can dictate her own rhythm and is unlikely to be harried into going faster than she wishes. The prominent types Sharetheknowledge and Sekavarma will look to sit in close attendance, but with such a crowded field the early positioning battle behind Chosen Princess will be intense. This race shape — a lone leader setting an honest but uncontested tempo — favours hold-up horses who can travel kindly in midfield and produce a sustained finish, as well as prominent racers who can draft off the pace and challenge from the second-last hurdle; this field holds considerably more hold-up types than can all get a clean run late, and Corkbeg, Scarlet Purse, Balinaboola Steel, The Ducks Walk and several others are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear will be hopelessly congested — of these, Corkbeg and The Ducks Walk are most likely to actually secure a workable position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Chosen Princess Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Chosen Princess bowls along uncontested and the prominent chasers cannot land close enough to mount a challenge.
scenarios.body: Chosen Princess controls the tempo entirely, the field strings out, and those tracking her in the first three are best placed entering the final flight; Sharetheknowledge and Sekakarma, both natural prominent racers, are ideally suited to draft off her and kick for home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Quickens Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady enough that a cluster of prominent-to-midfield runners arrive together from the second-last, turning it into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A genuine tactical race develops with multiple horses travelling strongly on the bridle at the top of the straight, suiting those with good finishing speed at this trip on Good ground; Sekakarma's consistent placed form in similar conditions and Torque De Lune's recent course-and-distance experience make them ideal beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create gaps for a late finisher to exploit.
scenarios.body: Chosen Princess goes faster than expected — perhaps due to the large field crowding her — and the race sets up for a horse with stamina and a late burst; Warm In Gorey's seven placed efforts in similar conditions and Cruisin Susan's recent placed form at the trip are relevant, though both must overcome traffic in a 17-runner field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Late
scenarios.trigger: If Chosen Princess is overwhelmed early by jostling rivals or tires abruptly, leaving no reliable lead and a muddling finish.
scenarios.body: A ragged, stop-start gallop produces a bunched finish that rewards whoever gets the clearest passage rather than the most talented runner; Duke Otto, who has form when conditions allow a prominent pitch and is at the top of the weights with experience, could benefit from any positional fortune.

watchPoints.text: Chosen Princess must be monitored from the outset — if she is harried on the first circuit by jostling rivals in this 17-runner field, the anticipated controlled pace evaporates and the entire race shape changes.

Sekakarma ran just nine days ago and Darragh O'Keeffe will need to manage his energy carefully; if the horse is flat from the quick turnaround, the prominent-racer scenario loses one of its two strongest protagonists.
Fenno's Soldier returning from 1,345 days off is a significant safety concern at a hurdle track — watch for jumping errors from this runner that could impede others in the middle of the field.

The redistributed hold-up horses (Corkbeg, Balinaboola Steel, The Ducks Walk, Scarlet Purse) will all be seeking gaps in a 17-runner field in the straight — a wall of horses is likely at the final flight and interference is a real possibility.

P J Rothwell has two runners (Little Boy Sivola, Warm In Gorey) and the yard is 3/13 in the last 14 days — watch for stable market moves between now and the off as an indicator of which runner the yard is sweetest on.

races.name: Traynors Of Wexford Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Forceonmyown
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 7yo for Gordon Elliott whose recent form is patchy (best finish 3rd over hurdles), but handles Good ground and this trip is within range; jockey Danny Gilligan is a journeyman booking that adds little confidence.|

runners_data.name: Something Fabulous
runners_data.note: John McConnell's 6yo has a win and three placings from five starts on Good ground, ran 3rd just 12 days ago, and Alex Harvey is a competent claiming rider — strong tactical profile for a race run at a controlled pace.|

runners_data.name: Clody Diamond
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's 6yo has a hurdle placing on Good ground and returns after 59 days off; headgear flag (h) noted, and she is a genuine prominent type who is capable of front-end placing if jumping is tidy.|

runners_data.name: Ellens Pride
runners_data.note: Curling's 6yo is a true hold-up horse by style, placed to midfield on the map only because the rear of the field is overcrowded — her actual racing pattern will likely see her last or near-last, and her recent form of 0-4-P-7-6 on Good ground gives little reason for confidence.|

runners_data.name: Lakewood Rose
runners_data.note: Trainer-jockey combination is amateur/family affair and unreliable form (all starts in 19-21f range), but the 8yo has consistency on Good ground and could be competitive if the closers get their race.|

runners_data.name: Nancy Wheeler
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish, which is a significant concern over 3m; all four starts on Good ground have produced finishes of 8th, 15th, 11th, and 14th — the form figures make her very difficult to recommend tactically.|

runners_data.name: Pacy Macie
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with two runs on Good ground returning the best form figures in this category (3rd at 24f, 6th at 25f); amateur jockey booking limits confidence but the staying profile suits the trip if she can get close enough.|

runners_data.name: Queen Of The Gales
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with going listed as UNKNOWN and 96 days since last run; the P-3-3-1-2 form string suggests progressive ability, and a fresh horse for Colin Motherway could be ahead of the assessor on this evidence.|

runners_data.name: Star Cave
runners_data.note: Headgear flag (ht) and an unknown style on limited evidence; one placing on Good ground at 24f but finished 9th on Soft — the profile is uncertain and the inexperienced 5lb claimer Eoghan Finegan adds to the risk.|

runners_data.name: Talladega
runners_data.note: Colin Bowe's 5yo is the confirmed front-runner but carries a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93, multiple pulled-up runs in form, and just one 4th and one 5th from two Good-ground starts over this sort of trip — the lead may not be sustained to the line.|

runners_data.name: Thornbury Queen
runners_data.note: No public form available to assess; headgear flag (h) and unknown going preference mean this runner carries the highest uncertainty in the field and must be treated as a complete unknown quantity.|

runners_data.name: Where Eagles Fly
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type who unseated and bolted in recent starts before a 7th on Good ground; 74 days since last run and a 7lb claimer in the saddle — the jumping reliability is the primary concern over 3m.|

runners_data.name: Burning Like Fire
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's 4yo is the youngest in the field and is flagged as fading in the finish; ran 14th on Good ground in sole comparable start and the prominent style with a fade profile is a liability over this stamina-testing trip.|

races.paceDynamic: Talladega is the one confirmed front-runner and, on Good ground over 3m at Wexford, is likely to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without genuine pace pressure from any comparable rival. The three prominent types — Forceonmyown, Something Fabulous, and Burning Like Fire — will track closely behind, creating a compact early order that keeps the tempo honest without turning the race into a cavalry charge. The field contains more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear: Ellens Pride is a genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map but will likely race even further back than shown, reducing her effectiveness in a shape where the race is controlled from the front. With one leader setting a measured pace and several prominent types able to travel economically in behind, this race shape favours horses with a prominent or close-tracking profile who can attack from the second-last hurdle — genuine hold-up horses face a stiffer task if the early fractions are not searching enough to string the field out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Talladega dictates a steady, uncontested gallop and the prominent trackers conserve energy for a run from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Talladega sets fractions that suit those immediately behind, and Something Fabulous or Forceonmyown — both travelling prominently on Good ground they handle — are ideally placed to pounce in the straight without having expended reserves chasing the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Fades, Tracker Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If Talladega's front-running effort takes its toll late and the horse fades, gifting the race to a close-tracking type who has been patient.
scenarios.body: Talladega's form shows multiple pulled-up runs and its style-fit is flagged, meaning its front-running may not be sustainable over the full 3m; a prominent type sitting just off the pace like Something Fabulous or Clody Diamond would then inherit a winning position without having led.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Make Late Ground
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften the leaders and hold-up horses can make sustained late progress on Good ground.
scenarios.body: Pacy Macie and Lakewood Rose both have form over similar distances on Good ground and could pick off tired rivals in the straight, though the measured pace typical of a mare's maiden at this trip makes this scenario less likely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Type Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced unknowns — Queen Of The Gales or Thornbury Queen — produces a step forward that their limited form has not yet revealed.
scenarios.body: Queen Of The Gales showed placed form in her last two starts and has had a break of 96 days that could have brought improvement, while Thornbury Queen has no public hurdles form to assess; either could outrun their map position if the talent is there.

watchPoints.text: Talladega's jumping must be monitored from the first hurdle — multiple pulled-up runs in form suggest stamina or jumping frailty, and if it makes a serious error it could unsettle the entire front group.|
Something Fabulous ran just 12 days ago and Alex Harvey must manage the horse carefully through the early stages if residual fatigue is not to show in the closing stages of a 3m maiden.|

Ellens Pride will almost certainly race further back than the midfield position shown on the map — watch whether she can find any daylight on the run-in if the race develops at a modest tempo that does not spread the field.|

Queen Of The Gales returns from 96 days off with a form string suggesting genuine progression (win and placed); a market move before the off would be a meaningful signal given the uncertain going profile.|

The amateur jockey cluster is notable — Mr B J Walsh, Miss N Lockhead Anderson, Miss N C Hennessy, and Mr J P Collins all ride in this race, and any erratic jumping or positioning by one of them early could disrupt the shape of the entire field over the first two hurdles.|

races.name: Brendan Cullimore Electrical Rated Novice Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Le Coq Hardi
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's 7yo is the class horse here at OR-133 and boasts an excellent record on good ground (3 wins, 10 places from 15 similar-going runs); Darragh O'Keeffe knows this horse well and 29 days since his last run looks ideal — the front-running role is unchallenged here.

runners_data.name: Ma Jacks Hill
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's 6yo arrives 20 days fresh and a 7lb claim from Kevin Healy is a positive; his one win came on good ground over 2m and he races prominently, making him Le Coq Hardi's closest pursuer throughout — the step up to 2m3½f is the one query.

runners_data.name: Warriors Wood
runners_data.note: Andrew McNamara's hold-up performer has a tidy recent profile (1W, 2P from last 4 on good ground) and Daniel King rode him to his win; the concern is whether a steady pace set by Le Coq Hardi will generate enough of a gap for a late challenge over this trip.

runners_data.name: Femme Magnifique
runners_data.note: David Harry Kelly's 8yo mare has been in good form (2W from last 4 on good ground) but her natural prominent racing style is compromised in this field — with Le Coq Hardi and Ma Jacks Hill ahead of her, she is unlikely to get a forward berth and Danny Gilligan will have to adapt, which dilutes her chance.

runners_data.name: Beauforts Storm
runners_data.note: Timothy Doyle's 7yo has been consistently disappointing of late (four 7th-place finishes bracketing a fall in the last six starts) and a mark of OR-112, the lowest in the field, reflects that; the 7lb claimer Mr D Doyle takes the ride and his hold-up profile offers little in a race likely to be steadily run.

races.paceDynamic: Le Coq Hardi is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners and no horse genuinely pressuring him for the lead, Darragh O'Keeffe can dictate a comfortable, sustainable gallop from the front over this 2m3½f trip on good ground at Wexford. Femme Magnifique is a natural prominent racer but, with Le Coq Hardi occupying the front and Ma Jacks Hill also inclined to race up with the pace, Femme Magnifique is unlikely to secure its natural position and will be pushed back toward midfield. The result is a race where the early tempo is controlled rather than pressured, suiting horses who can travel close to a moderate pace and deliver a clean finish rather than those who need a searching gallop to make ground. This race shape favours prominent and close-travelling runners who can sit just off Le Coq Hardi's shoulder and pounce — Warriors Wood, who races from hold-up but has a strong record on good ground, is the chief beneficiary if the pace is too steady for the leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Le Coq Hardi Leads Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Le Coq Hardi controls the gallop unchallenged and the field settles into a rhythm behind him.
scenarios.body: O'Keeffe dictates throughout at a fair but manageable tempo, and the race becomes a test of jumping accuracy and class at the business end; Le Coq Hardi's OR-133 and strong good-ground record (13 out of 15 sim-going runs in the frame) make him the obvious winner in this shape. Ma Jacks Hill, sitting closest in behind, is best placed to capitalise if the leader tires.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just hot enough to stretch the leaders and Warriors Wood can produce a strong late run.
scenarios.body: Warriors Wood has won and placed consistently on good ground over similar trips and his hold-up style suits a scenario where the front two have given enough to leave a gap for a finisher. Daniel King can time a late challenge from off the pace, and Warriors Wood's 2m3f experience (4th over 22f, 3rd over 20f) gives confidence he gets the trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaos — Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Le Coq Hardi sets too slow a gallop and a late sprint develops, scrambling the order.
scenarios.body: A very slow early tempo could cause positional jostling from Ma Jacks Hill and Femme Magnifique approaching the final fence, fragmenting the race shape and opening the door for any horse with a quick jump. Ma Jacks Hill's one win came in this type of messy, bunched finish and Gordon Elliott's one winner from 37 runners in the last 14 days suggests selective deployment.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Causes Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Beauforts Storm produces a career-best and the race unfolds at a tempo that masks his limitations.
scenarios.body: Beauforts Storm has shown only glimpses of form (2nd over 16f on good) and his OR-112 leaves him well treated if everything fell right, but his recent string of 7s and a fall (U) make this deeply unlikely. Beauforts Storm would need the pace to be perfectly judged and all principals to underperform significantly.

watchPoints.text: Le Coq Hardi is the one to keep onside — if he jumps cleanly at the early fences and establishes his rhythm uncontested, he could easily dictate this race from flag to finish and prove very hard to peg back.

Femme Magnifique's jockey Danny Gilligan will need to make a quick decision at the start — if she gets shuffled back early in a small field, her chances reduce sharply given she is not a natural hold-up horse.
Ma Jacks Hill's stamina for 2m3½f is unproven — his best form has come over 2m on good ground and Kevin Healy must judge carefully how much petrol is left if he follows Le Coq Hardi throughout.

With only five runners on good ground at Wexford, jumping errors will be magnified — Beauforts Storm's recent unseated rider (U in form) flags a jumping risk that could cause interference in a small field at a critical fence.
The trainer strike rate for Timothy Doyle (0 from 2 in last 14 days) and Andrew McNamara (1 from 4) are worth monitoring against Henry De Bromhead's stronger recent profile heading into this race.

races.name: Dan & Breda Byrne Memorial Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Farrokh
runners_data.note: In cracking form off a 37-day break, winning last time on good ground over 2m — Barry Connell's runner wants to race prominently and the trip extension to 2m3½f suits a horse that stays well; Sean Flanagan's positional judgment will be key navigating the crowded early stages.
runners_data.comment: Farrokh won last time out and has run over today's trip and conditions before, lending him some solid claims; the 37-day gap and a hefty 166 lb to carry are the chief questions to resolve.

runners_data.name: Sammy Smart
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran trained by Gibney who has course experience at Wexford and handles good ground adequately; his form figures of 3-8UP8 suggest inconsistency, and at 10 he must show he retains enough spark, but he stays the trip and Darragh O'Keeffe is an excellent tactical pilot.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Sammy Smart at least has experience of today's trip and going to call on, and at 166 lb he faces a stiff ask — yet our rating just about edges him ahead of his rivals, making him the one to side with.

runners_data.name: Catalani
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed pace-setters — won over 2m3f last time on good ground and Jack Foley's yard is in fair form (T14: 1/4); the 7lb claimer Mr B T Stone aboard is an unknown quantity at this level, and being taken on hard for the lead by Kasper Hauser could compromise his chance significantly.
runners_data.comment: Catalani arrives in cracking form, winning last time out and placing in two of the three starts before that, and his experience on today's going is a further asset; the weight burden of 165 lb is the one factor worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Kasper Hauser
runners_data.note: The highest-rated runner in the field (OR 114) and a genuine front-runner who has won his last two starts on good ground; the 5lb claim of Hogan helps at the weights, and at just four years old he has natural class over these rivals, though Coleman's 10-day turnaround (LR: 15d) warrants minor monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Kasper Hauser arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and shaped with promise when third three starts back, making him a potent force here; carrying 163 lb off a mark of 114 is the chief concern against him.

runners_data.name: Luimneach
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won over 2m on good ground 35 days ago for Conor O'Dwyer, ridden by the trainer's son Charlie (3lb claim); the tongue-tie is a regular fitment and he acts on this going, though he has not always been foot-perfect in the past and a clean round of jumping is essential for his finishing effort to count.
runners_data.comment: Luimneach arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, making him a clear threat on our third-best rating; the main concern is that two of his last five starts brought a pull-up and a fifth, highlighting some inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Giant Haystacks
runners_data.note: Prominent-running type for Ross O'Sullivan whose best recent form includes a win at 2m4f on good ground; the tongue-tie is regular fitment and he steps back up marginally in trip, though the O'Sullivan yard is cold over the past 14 days (T14: 0/20) which must temper expectations despite his solid profile.
runners_data.comment: Showed he can win at this level when scoring two starts back, but has disappointed since and returns after 31 days with a trainer who has drawn a blank in 20 attempts over the past fortnight; 161 lb is no help either.

runners_data.name: The Burrow
runners_data.note: 126-day absence makes him the chief fitness question in the field — his form string of /9569- shows no wins and no placed efforts in recent starts, and although he handles good ground, his consistent positioning near the rear of the field makes him reliant on a truly strong pace to deliver a meaningful late challenge.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked second-bottom of our figures here, The Burrow faces a stiff task carrying 159 lb on a lengthy 126-day absence, though he does have experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Chosen Shant
runners_data.note: In-form 10-year-old who has won twice in recent starts and placed four times on similar going, ridden by the experienced Phillip Enright; the hood is a regular fitment and at OR 93 he carries the lightest competitive burden among the prominent runners, which is a real tactical asset if he can find a clear passage 2-3 out.
runners_data.comment: Chosen Shant won three starts back and was second two starts back, but dropped to fifth last time out and carries a hefty 153 lb here; she has run over today's trip and going, and her profile suggests she's capable but this weight makes life harder.

runners_data.name: Auntie Lacey
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's six-year-old is held up off the pace and has consistent good-ground form but no wins in her last five; the hood and tongue plate are established headgear, and at 59 days since her last run she is fresh — Richard Deegan will need to find a run between 2 out and the last in what promises to be a bunched finish.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Auntie Lacey faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and going before, but a 59-day absence and a burden of 151 lb make it hard to fancy her fortunes improving.

runners_data.name: Stily
runners_data.note: Solid recent form including two thirds and a second at decent level — in reality a prominent-racing type who has been pushed to midfield on the map because the pace positions are overcrowded in this field; the hood is a regular fitment, good-ground record is strong (14/15), and if Philip Donovan can find a handy berth early his chance improves markedly, though racing out of role tempers the win expectation.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Stily is hard to fancy here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and the 25-day break at least suggests he arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Kasper Hauser and Catalani are the two confirmed front-runners in this 10-runner field, and with both intent on leading, there will be a genuine contest for supremacy from the outset over 2m3½f on good ground at Wexford. That early friction should produce an honest, unrelenting gallop — not a dawdle — which will stretch the field out and place a premium on stamina and jumping accuracy through the final circuit. The congestion in the prominent zone is significant: Farrokh, Sammy Smart, Giant Haystacks, and Chosen Shant all want to race prominently behind the two leaders, creating a tight, pressured group 2-3 out where traffic interference and jumping errors become genuine hazards. This race shape — a genuine pace with a bunched prominent group — favours a well-positioned, relaxed traveller with a clean jumping record who can slot into a handy spot without burning energy, or a true hold-up horse with enough stamina to pick off rivals late; pure speed-merchants who need to lead will find the pressure unsustainable. The field contains more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Stily is a genuine prominent racer who is most likely squeezed back into midfield, with Farrokh and Kasper Hauser best placed to actually secure the positions closest to the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Kasper Hauser and Catalani burn each other out setting a relentless gallop, leaving the prominent stalkers to pounce.
scenarios.body: The contested lead drains both front-runners in the final mile, handing the initiative to horses like Farrokh and Chosen Shant who travel prominently without over-committing early; their ability to conserve energy behind a hot pace and then sustain a run to the line makes them the chief beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner — most likely Kasper Hauser — establishes a clear lead early and controls the pace to suit, throttling back before the final bend.
scenarios.body: Kasper Hauser's recent back-to-back wins, youth (4yo), and good-ground form suggest he has the class and the lungs to dictate a sustainable gallop that suits his profile; if Catalani fades or takes a jump poorly, Kasper Hauser can dictate from the front and repel all challengers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swings Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong throughout, depleting the prominent group, allowing a true hold-up runner to scythe through beaten horses from 2 out.
scenarios.body: Luimneach has won on good ground over this sort of trip and is ridden by a claiming rider who can afford to be patient; Auntie Lacey, trained by Paul Nolan and handled by Deegan, also drops in from hold-up angles and could benefit if the prominent bunch ties up spectacularly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scramble, Congestion Costs
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors and traffic chaos at the third-last scatter the prominent group, producing a messy finish with a surprise outcome from a midfield position.
scenarios.body: The sheer density of horses racing between 3rd and 6th early on makes a trouble-in-running scenario plausible; Sammy Smart and Giant Haystacks, who are both proven course-and-distance types capable of staying on at their own pace, could find daylight late if the principals interfere with each other.

watchPoints.text: Kasper Hauser and Catalani — watch the first two fences carefully; if both commit fully to the lead with no concession, the pace could become injurious, dramatically shortening the chance of either winning and opening the race up for stalkers.

Prominent congestion between Farrokh, Sammy Smart, Giant Haystacks, Chosen Shant, and Stily (displaced) — at the cross-fence on the final circuit, 2-3 out, this group will be tightly bunched and any jumping error or bumping incident could end the race for multiple contenders simultaneously.

The Burrow — a 126-day absence with a poor recent form string; if he is ring-rusty early and takes a jumping mistake at a fence, he could cause interference to hold-up horses Luimneach and Auntie Lacey tracking behind him.

Catalani's amateur rider Mr B T Stone (7lb claim) — watch whether he can handle the pressure of Kasper Hauser attacking the lead; a novice error at a fence while battling for supremacy at the front is a material risk in a 10-runner handicap chase.

Chosen Shant — at OR 93 carrying 153lbs, one of the lightest burdens in the field, and Phillip Enright is adept at timing prominent runs; watch whether he can ghost into a handy position without getting boxed in behind the pace group in the early stages.

races.name: Racing Again October 25th & 26th Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: North Of Nashville
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a win at 26f on Good ground 37 days ago, and Colin Bowe's yard is showing 0/2 in the past fortnight; headgear worn, similar-going form reads 2 wins and 2 placed from 15 runs, but the race shape makes late-run angles harder to execute here.
runners_data.comment: Rated top of the field and carrying 166 lb, North Of Nashville arrives on the back of a win three starts back, bringing solid distance-and-going experience to her claims; the worry is her last two outings — a pull-up and a seventh — suggest she needs to recapture that form sharply.

runners_data.name: Thewaybackhome
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who wants to race prominently and has a solid recent record of placed efforts on Good ground; trainer T14 shows 1/6, John Shinnick takes the ride, and at 14 days' turnaround the horse is fresh enough to be competitive from the front rank.
runners_data.comment: Thewaybackhome has run over today's trip and going, and that second two starts back shows he can get competitive, but he remains winless in his last five and a career-high 158 lb is no small ask for a gelding ranked seventh of sixteen.

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: Thirteen-year-old with remarkable recent form — three wins in last six and a 15/15 record on similar going — racing off OR 88 with headgear (tb); Eoghan Finegan (5lb claim) adds appeal and the 7-day turnaround is clearly not a concern given the horse's recent busy schedule.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 16 on our figures and 8 lb below his official mark in our assessment, Fr Gilligansvoyge is hard to fancy despite a lively recent record that includes three wins in his last six starts; the weight of 157 lb adds further concern.

runners_data.name: Je Suis
runners_data.note: Prominent-style mare who has been out of the frame more often than not this season (-P350P) but steps back up to a longer trip where she was placed at 26f; the 7lb claimer Miss Lockhead Anderson rides and the headgear (tongue strap) may help, though the form line makes her hard to enthuse about.
runners_data.comment: Je Suis arrives on the back of a pulled-up effort eight days ago, but her experience over today's trip and going, combined with a rating of 94 that ranks her second in this field, marks her out as a leading contender; the risk is that she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Charlie's Gift
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose recent form reads poorly (7-7FP8) including a fall, and the six-year-old remains unexposed over 3m1f; Jordan Canavan rides for a yard at 0/2 over the past fortnight and the horse's jumping reliability is a concern in a large field.
runners_data.comment: Charlie's Gift has a troubled recent profile — falling and pulling up in consecutive starts before an eighth last time out — and yet to win in his last five, he faces a stiff task off 156 lb, though experience on today's going and a rating of 91 offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Cullenwaine
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer in sharp recent form — second in last run and a win before that — with a strong Good-ground record of 12/15 similar-going appearances; Shane O'Callaghan's 3lb claim helps at the weights and the horse looks the most dangerous tracker to Oogum Boogum.
runners_data.comment: Cullenwaine ran second last time out and was a winner two starts back, so he arrives in form, though he has run over today's trip and going before and the weight of 155 lb and a rating of 84 in a 16-runner field are limiting factors.

runners_data.name: Hit The Frame
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after a 104-day absence, which is the longest break in the field; showed a fall in recent form and trainer J P Flavin is 0/4 in the past fortnight, though the horse has a win at 25f on Good ground and stays the trip.
runners_data.comment: A winner five starts back, Hit The Frame has since posted a pair of fourths around a fall and a seventh in recent starts, suggesting consistency is the issue. He has run over today's trip and going, but 104 days off the track and a hefty 155 lb ask make confidence hard to muster.

runners_data.name: Stormy Master
runners_data.note: Veteran at 12 who wants to race off the pace, but the going — Good — slightly dries out his best conditions (three career wins have been on softer); his experience over big fields and 22 fences gives him jumping reliability even if his form reads 70-398 recently.
runners_data.comment: Stormy Master showed when third three starts back that he retains ability, and with experience over today's trip and going, plus 24 days of freshness, the gelding is weighted to outrun his official mark of 84 despite being winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Oogum Boogum
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner and the key pace-shaper; David Kenneth Budds is 2/3 over the past fortnight and Darragh O'Keeffe is a major booking, while a drop in weights off OR 82 suits — the horse's ability to control tempo uncontested is the defining factor for the entire race shape.
runners_data.comment: Oogum Boogum showed his best a winner and runner-up in his last six starts, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but back-to-back sevenths and eighths weigh against him despite a rating of 91 and a reasonable 24-day break.

runners_data.name: True Harmony
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse tagged as fading in the finish, and the form (8-9266) confirms this — has placed at 24f on Good ground but consistently weakens; Philip Donovan rides for a yard without a recent runner and the fading flag is a major negative at 3m1f.
runners_data.comment: True Harmony is winless in his last five starts, though a second three starts back shows he can get competitive, and he has run over today's trip and going; two consecutive sixth-place finishes weigh against him under 151 lb from a ranking of eleventh in the field.

runners_data.name: U Asking Me
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up racer whose last five runs include two pulled-ups and a fall (form -7P08F); the horse's natural rear-of-field position is already over-crowded, meaning it will likely be forced to race further forward than it prefers, which tempers its chance materially in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and with a fall among his recent outings, U Asking Me carries 147 lb and arrives on a quick 14-day turnaround; he has run over today's trip and going before, but his patchy profile makes him a tough one to trust.

runners_data.name: Mini Getaway
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who showed a win at 24f on Good and a placed effort recently; Alex Harvey takes the ride and the trainer sent out a winner from a single runner in the past 14 days — the horse stays this trip and its jumping record is consistent, making it a useful each-way interest if it travels well.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures and her recent form has been patchy, with three unplaced or minor finishes in her last four starts before a win four starts back; has run over today's trip and going, but it is hard to make a case for her at these weights.

runners_data.name: Urbs Intacta Manet
runners_data.note: Five-year-old whose career form on Good ground is modest (3/7 similar-going with no wins), and the finishing-fade flag reinforces that this lightly-raced horse doesn't see out trips well; its natural finishing position is at the back, yet the overcrowded hold-up group means it won't find that comfort zone easily.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 15 of 16 on our figures, Urbs Intacta Manet has a pulled-up to his name in recent form and little to recommend him beyond going experience and a fitness edge at 18 days since his last run.

runners_data.name: Three County Star
runners_data.note: Another five-year-old with a fade-in-finish flag and a form string of -056P9 — not a single win to its name and a pulled-up run in the last five; naturally a hold-up horse consigned to a midfield map position, the trip looks beyond it and the youth of the horse relative to the fences count against it.
runners_data.comment: Three County Star arrives in good order on 18 days' rest, has experience over today's trip and conditions, and our rating of 93 marks him out as a serious threat in this field — but a run of modest finishes in recent starts, including a pull-up, is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Barely Made It
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a placed effort (3rd) at 24f on Good ground as recently as 37 days ago, riding off OR 72 for Colin Bowe — same yard as North Of Nashville; forced to race out of its deepest comfort zone given the crowded rear, but the horse's calm, workmanlike style at least means it shouldn't panic at an unfamiliar position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 14 of 16 on our figures, Barely Made It faces a stiff ask here, though she does return on experience over today's trip and going, and a third last time out offers a sliver of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Tennesse Boy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old whose last three runs are all pulls-up (form 20-PPP), and the fade-in-finish flag compounds that grim record; Robert Tyner's yard has had no runners in the past 14 days, and this horse's chance relies entirely on something dramatic going wrong in front of it.
runners_data.comment: Tennesse Boy has pulled up in three of his last five starts and is winless in that sequence, with only a second two runs further back offering any encouragement; ranked last on our figures and carrying 141 lb, he faces a stiff task here.

races.paceDynamic: Oogum Boogum is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner field and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, Darragh O'Keeffe can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this extended 3m1f trip on Good ground. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which naturally compresses the race into the home straight and makes it harder for pure hold-up horses to generate the momentum they need to close down a fresh leader. Fr Gilligansvoyge, Cullenwaine, Thewaybackhome and Je Suis all want to race prominently and will fight to track Oogum Boogum from the front rank; given the depth of competition for the early positions, one or more of those four will land directly on the leader's heels and keep some pressure on without forcing a true burn-up. This race shape — an uncontested gallop at a steady-to-fair clip — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently, jump well and sustain their effort over the final mile, rather than hold-up types who need a truly genuine pace to reel in the leaders. It should be noted that the field contains a cluster of genuine hold-up horses — U Asking Me, Urbs Intacta Manet, Three County Star, Barely Made It and Tennesse Boy — who have been mapped to midfield because the rear of the race is over-subscribed; in reality, Oogum Boogum and Fr Gilligansvoyge are best placed to secure their natural positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Oogum Boogum Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Oogum Boogum secures an uncontested lead and the pace stays honest-but-manageable to the final fence.
scenarios.body: Darragh O'Keeffe sets a rhythm that suits Oogum Boogum's stamina profile and the field strings out behind, leaving hold-up horses with too much to make up; the prominent-tracking horses who stay closest travelling well are best placed to pounce if the leader tires.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Wears Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent-racing chasers travels sweetly in second or third and outstays Oogum Boogum from the final fence.
scenarios.body: Fr Gilligansvoyge's consistent recent form — three wins in five on Good ground at similar trips — makes it the most dangerous tracker, while Cullenwaine's sharp recent handicap victory and proven Good-ground record give it similar credentials to pounce late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is stronger than expected, the field spreads wide jumping and genuine closers find daylight in the home straight.
scenarios.body: North Of Nashville has winning form at this sort of trip on Good ground and carries headgear, making it the most credible late finisher in the field; Barely Made It, though forced out of its natural position, showed a placed effort at 24f on Good ground recently.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Thins The Field
scenarios.trigger: If the fences take a heavy toll in a big 16-runner field and several prominent fancies fall or unseat.
scenarios.body: With Charlie's Gift carrying a fall in recent form (7-7FP8) and Hit The Frame showing an F in its record, jumping errors by key fancies could open the door for a course-fresh, reliable jumper to inherit a position; Stormy Master's experience and Je Suis's solid record at this trip give them survival value.

watchPoints.text: Oogum Boogum — if Darragh O'Keeffe takes an uncontested lead and is allowed to bowl along at his own rhythm, he becomes the race-shaper and a live danger throughout; watch whether any prominent rival challenges him in the first mile.

Fr Gilligansvoyge — three wins in six recent runs and a flawless record on similar going make it the horse most likely to track the leader into contention; watch where Eoghan Finegan positions it jumping the first fence.
Charlie's Gift — has a fall in its recent form and races in a 16-runner field over 21 fences; a jumping error early could compromise several horses' races given the crowded early field.

The redistribution cluster (U Asking Me, Urbs Intacta Manet, Three County Star, Barely Made It, Tennesse Boy) — five genuine hold-up horses competing for rear positions will cause early jostling; watch for any of these being forced wide or into unfamiliar forward positions in the first mile.

Cullenwaine — Shane O'Callaghan's 3lb claim and a recent win on Good ground make this the most value-oriented watch in the prominent group; if it settles second or third and travels comfortably to three out, it becomes a serious contender.
